identity.name: Tarcondimotid Kingdom
alt_names: Client kingdom of Anazarbus and Castabala

land.text: Upper Cilicia: 'Anazarbus and Castabala, plus the regions of Bryclice, Characene, and Lacanitis, and ... strongholds on Mount Amanus' (the 66-63 BC holdings on the page)

successors.note: 'Philopator II, the last Tarcondimotid king, died. Tiberius then incorporated the territory into the Roman provincial system.'

capitals.name: Castabala (Hierapolis-Castabala)
capitals.note: 'Castabala may have been the original capital' (Tarcondimotus I page): a hedge, for the years before the royal mint at Anazarbus. The page gives no coordinates; those are the site's, from the researcher.

capitals.name: Anazarbus (Anavarza)
capitals.note: 'Castabala may have been the original capital. Anazarbus, the site of the royal mint, later served as the administrative center'; Tarcondimotus II 'refounded the capital, Anazarbos, as Caesarea' in 19 BC. The page gives no coordinates.

rulers.name: Tarcondimotus I
rulers.title: toparch of Upper Cilicia from c. 70 BC; king from c. 38 BC
rulers.note: 'formally recognized as king by Mark Antony c.38 BC'; 'died fighting on Antony's behalf at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC'. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the reign starts with the toparchy confirmed by Pompey 'in or after 66 BC' (body text); the infobox has the toparchy 'c. 70-38 BC'.]

rulers.name: Philopator I
rulers.title: toparch
rulers.note: 'His eldest surviving son, Philopator I, succeeded him as king. Octavian stripped the royal title within the year, but Philopator appears to have kept the toparch position.'

rulers.name: Tarcondimotus II
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: '20 BC: Augustus restored the royal title to Tarcondimotus II'; refounded Anazarbus as Caesarea in 19 BC. His death year is not on the page, so the end is a bridge.

rulers.name: Philopator II
rulers.title: king
rulers.note: 'AD 17: Philopator II, the last Tarcondimotid king, died.' The start of his reign is not on the page (bridge).

region.text: Upper Cilicia: 'Anazarbus and Castabala, plus the regions of Bryclice, Characene, and Lacanitis, and ... strongholds on Mount Amanus' (the 66-63 BC holdings on the page)

ledger.note: 66 BC or after: Pompey confirms Tarcondimotus as toparch of Upper Cilicia. 'was confirmed as toparch by Pompey in or after 66 BC'; 'confirmed in his holdings as part of Pompey's eastern settlement' (66-63 BC); 'The core of Tarcondimotus' territory comprised the cities of Anazarbus and Castabala', with Bryclice, Characene and Lacanitis (Tarcondimotus I page). The dossier starts here, not at the royal title of c. 38 BC (a rename under the one-state rule); the infobox gives the toparchy as 'c. 70-38 BC' and the body only 'in the early first century BC', so 66 is the earliest year the body supports ('in or after') and the real start may be later. The land is the researcher's reading of the page's holdings. [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x: was -38; the reviewer proposed about -64, which is not on the page.]

region.text: Upper Cilicia: 'Anazarbus and Castabala, plus the regions of Bryclice, Characene, and Lacanitis, and ... strongholds on Mount Amanus' (the 66-63 BC holdings on the page)

ledger.note: 66 BC or after: Upper Cilicia is a Roman client under Pompey's settlement. The page calls Tarcondimotus 'a Roman client ruler of Upper Cilicia' (lead) and names the dynasts Pompey confirmed 'client rulers subordinate to Rome', giving him the title of toparch, not king. The page does not use the word 'client' for his status under Antony, Octavian, Augustus or Tiberius, so the status is carried through to AD 17 as the lead's description. The roman-republic dossier has no event for it and should carry the mirror (vassal_start, counterpart tarcondimotid-kingdom, 66 BC). [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x: the reviewer proposed -38; the page ties the client status to Pompey's settlement.]

c. 38 BC: Mark Antony grants Tarcondimotus the royal title. 'Antony granted him the royal title c.38 BC' in recognition of his loyalty against the Parthian invasion of 40 BC (Tarcondimotus I page); Pompey 'did not recognize him as king'. The state and its land continue; the toparchy becomes a kingdom. The year is the page's approximate year. [Fix 2026-10-19: was the dossier's found event.]

31 BC: Tarcondimotus I dies at Actium and the royal title lapses. 'died fighting on Antony's behalf at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC'; his son Philopator I succeeded 'as king', but 'Octavian stripped the royal title within the year', Philopator keeping the toparch position. The land is unchanged.
